text.p: Following are the main stories from Austrian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Presse survey finds only 12 percent of Austrians believe that state pensions will be the same level in 10 years as they are now.
- Austria's lies in second bottom place in terms of the European Union's liberalisation of the telecoms industry.

- Austria Tabak will go public at the earliest in mid-October. A final decision is likely to come in the middle of next month, dependant on the stock market environment. A sale of 25 percent is planned, although this could be raised.
- The starting up of new enterprises is up 18 percent in the first half.
- 39 victims of paedophile abuse have now been identified in the pornography ring in the Salzkammergut.
- Austrian banks continue to loosen their tight opening times with Raiffeisenlandesbank Niederoesterreich-Wien having extended hours in all 70 bank branches.
- Unemployed can from now on earn on the side without being fined.
- Gasoline prices fall again but the next hike is looming. Super and normal petrol have become 20 groschen cheaper.
- Leykam is checking the possibility of an Indonesian partner.
- For the first time Austria has a trade deficit with the Czech Republic.
